title: Japan 40-Year JGB auction (¥300bn anticipated) — the tenor proposed as the BoJ taper's clean control, and the one where MOF cut issuance hardest
source: EST: mof.go.jp English November 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2611e.htm), re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 for this initial research (HTTP 200, 25,187 bytes) — its table row reads 'Nov. 25, 2026 | 40-year', and the same fetch was the basis of the jgb-20y-auction-2026-10-20 proposal that created this entry. NO SIZE IS ASSERTED: not one November row carries an announcement href on 2026-09-09, and MOF's own note at the foot of that page reads verbatim 'Each issue amount will be announced about one week prior to each auction date', putting terms around 2026-11-18. ¥300bn is the anticipated base case from a second MOF primary, the Auction Results for JGBs workbook (english/policy/jgbs/auction/past_auction_results/Auction_Results_for_JGBs.xls, 492,032 bytes, last saved 2026-08-13, re-downloaded and re-parsed 2026-09-09): the 40-year runs bi-monthly and issue 19 (3.8% coupon, maturity 2066-03-20) has been sold at ¥300bn at both its auctions so far, 2026-05-27 and 2026-07-22. Filed `estimate` on the two counts every JGB entry on this calendar records: the size is anticipated rather than announced, and market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office. The DATE is not in doubt — the estimate label is about the taxonomy and the unannounced size, not the evidence. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: Proposed 2026-09-09 by the jgb-20y-auction-2026-10-20 initial-research adjacency sweep (proposals/jgb-40y-auction-2026-11-25.from-jgb-20y-auction-2026-10-20.json, read as input and now shadowed by this canonical file); researched the same day (docs/research/events/jgb-40y-auction-2026-11-25.md). THE RESEARCH RETIRED THE PROGRAM IT WAS PROPOSED TO RUN. The proposal's design was: use the 40-year as the uncontaminated control for the BoJ's bucket taper (89.6% of its float sits in the untapered 'more than 25 years' bucket, reproduced exactly at 2026-11-25 this session), with the cover ratio as the outcome because this single-price tenor prints no tail. Both halves fail on measurement. (1) COVER CANNOT BE THE OUTCOME. Cover is a mechanical function of offering size, and the size relationship carries OPPOSITE SIGNS at control and treated tenor: regressing cover on ln(size) over all history gives the 40-year −1.080 (t = −7.39) against the 20-year +0.749 (t = +7.72). On the sibling ledger's own BoJ-keyed windows the cover DiD is −0.023 (t = −0.10) against the 20-year and −0.069 (t = −0.37) against the 30-year, with a minimum detectable effect of 0.52–0.62 cover points — five to six times any plausible effect. (2) THE CONTROL IS NOT A CONTROL. Over exactly the DiD window MOF cut the 40-year −44.6% (¥700bn → ¥388bn mean), against the 30-year's −22.9% and the 20-year's −18.8%; bid volume follows size at an elasticity of 0.75 (se 0.07) since 2019, so the tenor chosen as untreated received the LARGEST dose of the other policy. A control more treated than the treated arm identifies nothing. The one metric not pinned to issuance size — the clearing concession, highest accepted yield minus MOF's same-session par 40-year — does move: −2.28bp → +1.65bp, t = +5.08, DiD −4.05bp against the 20-year at t = −3.01, SIGN OPPOSITE to the bucket mechanism. It does not survive the adversarial pass: inside the window the 40-year par level rose 1.94% → 3.84% monotonically, and level-adjusting collapses the jump to +0.67bp (t = +0.77). Level and window are collinear at n = 8 + 8, so the design cannot separate them. WHAT SURVIVES AND IS USABLE: the 95-auction concession calibration of mean −0.25bp is STALE for the current regime — the eight auctions since 2025-05-28 run +1.65bp, and the two live conditions (¥300bn size, 25s30s at the 1.0th percentile of 5,501 sessions) both associate with a cheaper clearing. A November seasonality story was tested and killed the same way September's was (raw +0.288 cover, t = +1.46; neighbour-controlled +0.089, t = +0.56), as was a Japanese-holiday-week story (raw −0.224, t = −1.69; neighbour-controlled −0.168, t = −1.07). NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low` for the reasons all four sibling JGB ledgers record: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure, no house playbook is rates-keyed, and the auction-to-US-long-end channel is a null whose sign does not hold across samples. The date is additionally UNUSABLE for any spillover test: 2026-11-25 is the pre-Thanksgiving US data dump, carrying pce-2026-11-25 and gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25 (both high) plus beige-book, durable-goods, new-home-sales and treasury-7y-note on the same session. Two dated events PROPOSED in the same PR off primaries fetched this session: jpx-market-closure-2026-11-23 (JPX's own derivatives holiday-trading page, verbatim: 'Markets will not be opened on November 23, 2026 (Labor Thanksgiving Day) due to a JPX Group-wide BCP testing (disaster recovery testing) of FY 2026 which is planned to be implemented for November 21 through 23') and jgb-30y-auction-2026-11-10. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
